summary: The note surveys emerging trends in youth athletic performance training after September 2023: HIIT, wearable tech, year-round sport specialization, psychological training, regimented nutrition and supplements, loosely certified coaches, and rising costs. For each trend it pairs supporters' claims with concerns from health experts, parents and commentators. It closes by asking whether pushing young athletes this hard prioritizes performance over health and childhood.
one_line: An overview of new youth athletic training trends, such as HIIT, wearables, specialization and supplements, weighing claimed benefits against health, ethical and cost concerns.
key_facts: Jim Carter, a coach with over a decade at the Newfield Wildcats, introduced HIIT into his under-15 football program starting October 15, 2023.
Carter says of the HIIT shift: "The kids are more engaged, and we've seen a notable difference in their stamina."
Dr. Lillian Matthews warned on November 3 that children's developing bodies "might not be ready to withstand the kind of stress that HIIT introduces."
Jason Morales, a 14-year-old swimmer, has used a smartwatch since December 2023 that suggests personalized swimming programs; his coach is Terry Robinson.
Sports psychologist Dr. Marcus Renner argues wearable tech is "teaching kids to trust machines over their bodies."

Vanessa Hill, 12, has played only soccer since age eight, trains five days a week, follows a strict diet and attends off-season clinics; her coach Gary Stevenson believes specialization is key to professional success.
Pediatric orthopedic surgeon Dr. Susan Choi has treated increasing overuse injuries since early 2024, including repetitive stress injuries once seen only in adult athletes.
Psychological training took off after Dr. Aaron Heller's September 2023 statement on the benefits of mental training; parent Sarah Jennings objects, saying "They're just kids."
Marcy Adams, a 16-year-old volleyball player, follows a meal plan tailored to the calorie by a nutritionist hired by her team.
Dietitian Rick Donovan warns the supplement industry isn't regulated strictly enough and labels may not match bottle contents.
Blogger Mark Thompson criticized weekend-course and online-certified "performance coach" trainers on January 22, 2024.
The note says costlier programs, nutritionists, technology and psychological training create a socioeconomic divide favoring families with deeper pockets.
Retired professional athlete Antonio Spears asked in a February 10, 2024 interview: "Are we training young champions or are we stealing their childhood?"
